q: In 1905, Albert Einstein proposed that light must also be thought of as a particle or photon.
e: True. Einstein's 1905 photon is the particle side of light, energy hf. The year 1905 belongs to this fact, not a nearby discovery date.

q: In 1923, Louis de Broglie proposed that the wavelength of a material particle would be related to its kinetic energy directly.
e: False. The right claim is this: In 1923, Louis de Broglie proposed that the wavelength of a material particle would be related to its momentum. de Broglie wavelength is h over momentum; every moving particle carries a wave. The printed line wrongly says in 1923, Louis de Broglie proposed that the wavelength of a material particle would be related to its kinetic energy directly.

q: The wavelength associated with a moving particle is also called de Broglie wavelength.
e: True. de Broglie wavelength is h over momentum; every moving particle carries a wave. The wavelength associated with a moving particle is also called de Broglie wavelength.

q: All moving particles exhibit properties of both particles and waves nature.
e: True. All moving particles exhibit properties of both particles and waves nature.

q: The existence of matter waves were first experimentally confirmed by Michelson and Morley's experiment.
e: False. The right claim is this: The existence of matter waves were first experimentally confirmed by Thomson's cathode ray diffraction experiment and the Davisson-Germer experiment for electrons. In metals the mobile carriers are electrons, drifting opposite the conventional-current arrow. The printed line wrongly says the existence of matter waves were first experimentally confirmed by Michelson and Morley's experiment.

q: In an electron microscope, the wave nature of electrons is used instead of light.
e: True. In metals the mobile carriers are electrons, drifting opposite the conventional-current arrow. In an electron microscope, the wave nature of electrons is used instead of light.

q: Bohr's second postulate of hydrogen atom can be explained with the matter waves concept of electrons.
e: True. In metals the mobile carriers are electrons, drifting opposite the conventional-current arrow. Bohr is the name attached to this result.

q: An integral number of de Broglie wavelengths associated with a revolving electron must fit in the diameter of an orbit.
e: False. The right claim is this: An integral number of de Broglie wavelengths associated with a revolving electron must fit in the circumference of an orbit. In metals the mobile carriers are electrons, drifting opposite the conventional-current arrow. The printed line wrongly says an integral number of de Broglie wavelengths associated with a revolving electron must fit in the diameter of an orbit.

q: The de Broglie wavelength for a macroscopic particle like a basketball is much longer than that of an electron.
e: False. The right claim is this: The de Broglie wavelength for a macroscopic particle like a basketball is very much shorter than those of an electron, hence wave nature cannot be observed for a basketball. In metals the mobile carriers are electrons, drifting opposite the conventional-current arrow. The printed line wrongly says the de Broglie wavelength for a macroscopic particle like a basketball is much longer than that of an electron.

q: Because of its very short de Broglie wavelength, wave nature cannot be observed for a basketball.
e: True. de Broglie wavelength is h over momentum; every moving particle carries a wave. Short de Broglie wavelength, wave nature cannot be observed for a basketball.

q: 1 eV (electron volt) is the energy gained by an electron when accelerated through a potential of one thousand volts.
e: False. The right claim is this: 1 eV (electron volt) is the energy gained by an electron when accelerated through a potential of one volt. In metals the mobile carriers are electrons, drifting opposite the conventional-current arrow. The printed line wrongly says 1 eV (electron volt) is the energy gained by an electron when accelerated through a potential of one thousand volts.
